categories.name: Parliamentary Affairs
categories.definition: Covers the rules, procedures, and conduct of business within the House of Commons, including debates, points of order, privilege, committees, and the legislative process.

categories.name: Economic & Fiscal Policy
categories.definition: Concerns the management of the national economy, including budgets, taxation (e.g., GST), inflation, interest rates, government spending, and the national debt.

categories.name: Trade & Industry
categories.definition: Relates to domestic and international commerce, including trade agreements (e.g., Canada-US FTA), tariffs, foreign investment, support for specific industries, and corporate regulation.

categories.name: Social Policy
categories.definition: Pertains to the social safety net and public services, including unemployment insurance, pensions, health care, post-secondary education, housing, and family benefits.

categories.name: Justice, Rights & Immigration
categories.definition: Covers the legal system, civil liberties, and population management, including the Criminal Code, capital punishment, human rights, the Charter, immigration, and refugee policy.

categories.name: Agriculture & Natural Resources
categories.definition: Focuses on primary industries and the environment, including farming, fisheries, forestry, energy policy (e.g., National Energy Program), and resource transportation.

categories.name: Intergovernmental & Constitutional Affairs
categories.definition: Addresses the relationship between federal and provincial governments and the nation's foundational laws, including constitutional reform, federal transfers, and national unity.

categories.name: Foreign Affairs & Defence
categories.definition: Concerns Canada's role and relationships in the world, including diplomacy, defence policy (e.g., NATO), the armed forces, international aid, and peacekeeping.

categories.name: Government Operations & Ethics
categories.definition: Relates to the administration and accountability of the executive branch, including ministerial responsibility, Crown corporations, the public service, conflict of interest, and access to information.

categories.name: Indigenous & Northern Affairs
categories.definition: Focuses on issues concerning First Nations, Inuit, and Métis peoples and the governance of Canada's territories, including land claims, treaty rights, and the Indian Act.

natural_rationale: A 12-category taxonomy was chosen because the data reveals two very large and internally diverse policy domains in the 10-category model that benefit from being split. Separating 'Social Policy' into 'Labour & Employment' and 'Social Programs' isolates the recurring, high-frequency debates on unemployment and UI from other social issues like pensions and health. Similarly, splitting 'Justice, Rights & Immigration' into 'Criminal Justice' and 'Rights, Immigration & Citizenship' distinguishes debates about law and order from those concerning fundamental rights, immigration, and national identity, reflecting major, distinct streams of parliamentary discussion.
